# Text-to-speech model comparison

Bee Box can speak its chat replies aloud. The voice comes from a
text-to-speech model, and the box can use more than one. New speech models
ship often, so choosing one is a recurring decision. This page holds a
comparison made for that decision, in September and October 2026: nineteen
models read the same seven short texts, and one take of each is here to
listen to.

The box now speaks with OpenAI's gpt-4o-mini-tts by default, or with Gemini
3.8 Flash-Lite TTS, which takes the speaking style of the box's personality.

<!-- contents -->

## The models

<!-- models -->

Each model used one voice from its provider's standard list, named above. A
different voice of the same model can sound quite different, so a take shows
the model with that voice, not the model at its best. Cost per minute comes from every
successful take in the run, including pacing takes not on this page: for models reached through OpenRouter, the amount OpenRouter
billed; for the others, the list price applied to what was sent (characters,
or for Gemini on Google's API, the token counts the API returned).

## How it was tested

Each model read seven texts. Each text tests one thing a voice for the box
must do:

- **Pacing:** a long sentence with asides and a list in parentheses, read
  plain only: it tests the model's own phrasing. Rendered five times per
  model, because pauses vary from take to take. The page plays the take of
  middle length and gives the range of lengths. Three takes are enough for a
  new model.
- **Code-switching:** whole phrases in Spanish, German, and French inside an
  English sentence.
- **Single German words:** two German words inside an English sentence.
- **Sarcasm:** words that mean the opposite of what they say. Nothing in the
  text marks it, so only direction can make it sound sarcastic.
- **Relief, anger, exhaustion:** a mood the words already carry, to hear
  whether the model finds it without help.

Every model read every text **plain**: the text alone, with no direction.
Models that accept direction also read some texts **directed**, and a few
read them with **markup** (pauses, sighs, speed changes) as well. Each
backend takes direction in its own way, so the directed takes are not one
experiment repeated. Under each directed take, the page shows exactly what
was sent. The ways seen here:

- **A prose instruction in a separate field.** OpenAI's gpt-4o-mini-tts
  (`instructions`) and Gemini 3.8 (`speech_metadata.style`). The direction is
  not part of the text, so the model cannot read it aloud. tts-1-hd ignores
  instructions.
- **Prose or tags inside the text.** Gemini 3.1 takes a prose direction in
  front of the text, and free-form bracket tags such as `[sarcastically]`
  anywhere in it. ElevenLabs v3 and Fish Audio take free-form bracket tags.
  Direction inside the text can be read aloud as words. Gemini 3.8 reads
  bracket tags aloud, so the tag style that works on 3.1 fails on 3.8.
- **A value from a fixed list.** Cartesia (`generation_config.emotion`),
  MiniMax (an emotion option), and MAI-Voice-2 through OpenRouter (a `style`
  such as `angry` or `relieved`, with nothing for sarcasm or tiredness). One
  value applies to the whole take. Voxtral takes fixed `[emotion=…]` and
  `[pace=…]` tags inside the text, and pronunciation as IPA phones in a
  separate `phoneme_hints` field.
- **Events and spans.** Grok takes pauses, sighs, and spans such as
  `<slow>…</slow>` and `<soft>…</soft>`, but no emotion.
- **Nothing.** Deepgram Aura-2 and Flux and ElevenLabs Flash take no
  direction, so they read every text plain only. Flux infers delivery from the
  text by design.

Some controls were not tried: Azure's full SSML for MAI-Voice-2 (not
reachable through OpenRouter), ElevenLabs voice settings and pronunciation
dictionaries, Cartesia pronunciation dictionaries, and Voxtral's
`expressiveness`.

**The transcript check.** The first successful take of each model, text, and
variant was sent to a speech-to-text model. Its transcript was searched for
words of the direction that are not in the text, which means the model read
its direction aloud. The other differences between transcript and text are
not shown: nearly all were the transcriber's ("40" for "forty", the foreign
phrases respelled). The Voxtral takes were transcribed with OpenAI's
gpt-4o-transcribe. The transcriber used for the September takes is not
recorded.

The renders, the transcript check, and the script that rendered the Voxtral
takes are in the repository at
[research/tts-model-comparison](https://github.com/ianb/beebox/tree/main/research/tts-model-comparison).

## Direction read aloud

Direction inside the text can be spoken as words. The transcript check found
it in these takes. All are Gemini; Gemini 3.8 reads bracket tags aloud, and
Gemini 3.1 can read a prose direction in front of the text. The check sees
only words the transcriber wrote down, so a tag read aloud in a way the
transcriber dropped is not listed.
